newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to cut taxes for small and medium companies.
newsitem.headline: Spain to cut taxes for small and medium companies.

text.p: The ruling Spanish Popular party will present an amendment to the budget that will cut the tax rate on small- and medium-sized companies to 30 percent from 35 percent on initial earnings.

Commerce Secretary Jose Manuel Fernandez told Spanish National Radio on Tuesday that "the impact of the amendment will be very positive, since it tries to avoid the discrimation that has existed against small- and medium-sized businesses."
"(The measure) is part of all those steps favourable to the small- and medium-sized business that the PP has taken since assumed the government," Fernandez said.
The amendment establishes the tax cut for the initial 15 million in profits for those companies that invoice less than 250 million pesetas a year.
The rest of their profits, approximately half for businesses of this size, will continue to be taxed at the current 35 percent rate.
The measure will be applied from January of 1997 and is expected to cost the Exchequer some 20 billion pesetas.
